headline: Andhra Pradesh targets 50% women’s workforce participation
summary: Andhra Pradesh aims to increase women's workforce participation from 35.8% to 50% through job expansion in manufacturing, industry, and agriculture. Key drivers include expanding industrial hubs like Sri City and Brandix Apparel City, alongside scaling women's involvement in natural farming initiatives. While several upcoming projects are projected to create tens of thousands of jobs for women, the government has not specified a timeline for reaching the target.

headline: Tencent denies plans to cut half its workforce, says AI restructuring remarks were misinterpreted
summary: Tencent has refuted social media reports claiming it plans to cut half of its workforce following a strategic shift toward artificial intelligence. The company clarified that executive remarks were misinterpreted, explaining that resources are being divided equally between optimizing core operations and exploring AI-native growth opportunities. The restructuring focuses on flattening management and reallocating talent rather than mass downsizing.

headline: Acquelia Colaco takes charge as CPO at Omnicom Global Solutions
summary: Omnicom Global Solutions has appointed Acquelia Colaco as Chief People Officer for its India and Philippines operations. Based in Bengaluru, Colaco brings over 20 years of HR experience from previous leadership roles at firms including XBP Global, Tesco, Infosys, and IBM. In her new role, she will drive talent strategy, leadership development, and workforce transformation to support the company's expansion.

headline: Shaveta Kapoor moves to Leonardo DRS as CHRO
summary: Shaveta Kapoor has been named Chief Human Resources Officer at Leonardo DRS, where she will support business priorities and growth alongside CEO John Baylouny. She brings over 15 years of HR, M&A, and operational transformation experience, having previously served as CHRO at ASRC Federal and holding leadership roles at Serco. Kapoor earned her MBA from Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business.

headline: Sharad Mate takes charge of HR operations at Mahyco
summary: Sharad Mate has been appointed as the Head of HR Operations at Mahyco, where he will lead initiatives focused on process efficiency, HR digitisation, and operational agility. Mate has been with Mahyco for nearly seven years, most recently serving as an HR business partner managing plant operations and workforce strategy. Prior to Mahyco, he spent nearly 11 years at Varroc, building extensive expertise in manufacturing environments and industrial relations.

headline: Ranjeeka Sachdev to lead HR at BMW Group India
summary: BMW Group India has appointed Ranjeeka Sachdev as its new Chief Human Resources Officer to lead people strategy, talent transformation, and employee engagement. An alumna of IIM Ahmedabad, Sachdev brings over 23 years of HR leadership experience across multiple sectors, including previous senior roles at Jaquar Group and Pernod Ricard.

headline: PVH to cut around 1,040 jobs globally, targeting office-based roles
summary: PVH Corp, the parent company of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, is eliminating roughly 1,040 corporate jobs, representing 4% of its global workforce and 12% of office-based roles. The workforce reduction is part of the company's broader PVH+ strategy aimed at streamlining operations and creating a more efficient cost structure. The restructuring follows a weak financial performance in the second quarter, where PVH reported a $102.9 million net loss alongside declining sales.

headline: Tata Power grants 64.88 lakh stock options to eligible employees
summary: Tata Power has granted nearly 64.89 lakh stock options to eligible employees under its ESOP 2023 plan at an exercise price of Rs 360 per share. The options will vest over a period of one to three years, allowing employees to acquire equity as the company continues its operational expansion. This initiative coincides with Tata Power investing approximately Rs 10,000 crore in capital expenditure during the first half of FY27 across renewable energy and infrastructure projects.

headline: PLI schemes generate just 28% of targeted jobs, raising questions over manufacturing employment
summary: A NITI Aayog assessment reveals India’s Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have created only 28% of their 3 million targeted jobs by FY26, despite reaching 76% of investment goals. While sectors such as electronics and pharmaceuticals are performing well, the overall shortfall highlights that capital investment does not automatically result in immediate job creation. The report recommends moving away from uniform policy frameworks toward sector-specific adjustments combined with demand-side incentives.

headline: The career advantages nobody teaches you to cultivate
summary: Human resources executives emphasize that subtle skills—such as compelling storytelling, empathetic listening, and accepting strategic lateral moves—often drive long-term career progression more than technical qualifications alone. Developing these less obvious qualities helps professionals effectively communicate ideas, build trust, and gain broader business perspectives.

headline: Rising Star: Kavita Kulwant on why AI should take the administrative load, not the human responsibility
summary: Kavita Kulwant, a total rewards professional at Tata Consultancy Services, has developed two AI agents to automate routine administrative HR tasks. By shifting clerical workloads to AI, her initiative aims to create capacity for HR teams to focus on strategic problem-solving and deeper employee engagement. Kulwant advocates for using technology to streamline data processing while keeping human judgment and empathy at the center of organizational decision-making.

headline: Yugavel Manickam is now CHRO, Suguna Foods
summary: Yugavel Manickam has been appointed as the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO) at Indian poultry conglomerate Suguna Foods. Prior to this role, he served as the group HR head for the Cooling division at Thermax. Manickam brings extensive leadership experience from previous HR positions at Saint-Gobain, Wittur Group, EID Parry, and Reliance Retail.
